## Prior defects

| Defect | Independent finding |
|---|---|
| Standard urllib response/reader shape | **Closed by transport replacement.** The candidate no longer introspects urlopen().fp.fp; it feeds a deadline-aware socket adapter to http.client.HTTPResponse, whose makefile(\"rb\") returns a BufferedReader. The candidate’s loopback response test passes. Running that same regression against the prior parent fails with OSError: Bright Data response stream does not expose bounded reads (logs/parent-reader-regression.log). |
| Content-Length and chunk framing reads | **Closed.** Every raw refill passes through _DeadlineSocket.recv_into, which recomputes remaining time and applies it before the blocking socket read. Candidate tests pass for slow Content-Length bodies, chunk data, CRLF, trailers, and HTTP error bodies. |
| Connection and response-header deadline | **Not fully closed.** Response-header parsing is bounded by the deadline adapter. connection.connect() runs before that adapter is installed and receives only the timeout calculated once at hop start. The deterministic offline HTTPS setup probe modeled two connect phases, each shorter than that original timeout: a 1.0s budget elapsed to 1.2s before the code noticed expiry. It suppressed the HTTP request, but the blocking connection setup itself exceeded the task deadline. Name resolution can also block outside socket timeouts. See logs/independent-probes.log. |
| Redirect count, credentials, methods, expiry | **Partly closed.** Current provider GET/POST hops are counted, cross-origin Authorization is stripped, POST is converted to GET for 301/302/303, 307/308 preserve method/body, and the target HTTP request is suppressed after expiry. Offline tests cover count, stripping and expiry. The rewrite is unconditional for 301/302/303: a deterministic probe shows HEAD and DELETE also become GET (and DELETE’s body is dropped). The generic transport therefore does not preserve method semantics safely for those inputs. |
